quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, what should they do?

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time on a two-lane road. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider starts.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may interfere with the turn signals.
It may be hard to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to keep your balance.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by moving only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield should have all of these qualities except:
questions.explanation: A good eye shield should be free of scratches, resist penetration, close securely, and allow air to pass through. It does not need to be airtight.

questions.question: When stopping a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medicines for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies make you drowsy and may make riding unsafe. Check how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: Using arms to hold body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what is usually best to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of a lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track often works best.

questions.question: To make good decisions in traffic, what do you need to do first?
questions.explanation: Always look ahead on the road to spot hazards before you reach them. Be aware of everything around your motorcycle.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. A mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and to the side is most important.

questions.question: What should you do to increase your visibility?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible: wear bright or reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Which formation keeps group riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps a group close while letting each rider have safe space around them. Use single-file for curves, turns, and entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: What does eye contact with a driver mean?

options.text: Does not mean they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not notice them.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after it has been in a crash?
questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been in a crash.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch for hazards behind you.

questions.question: When slowing down to a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use less throttle and apply only the front brake.
Shift down through the gears as you slow.
Pull in the clutch and coast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears as you slow.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Always use both brakes when braking.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk occurs at intersections. Be extra alert where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Downshifting to a lower gear slows down your motorcycle.
